events.name: Someone Is Following You
events.intro:
{lead} stops and looks back down the path, ears up.
You look too. Nothing. A bush, moving, with no wind to move it.

success.text: {lead} keeps glancing back for a while. Then, reluctantly, it lets it go.
Nobody answers. The bush stops moving, very suddenly, the way bushes do not.

events.name: Someone Is Following You: A Hat
events.intro: A hat, behind a wall. The wall is too low. Most of a person is visible behind it, crouching, very still.

success.text: You walk past. The hat turns slowly to follow you.

events.name: Someone Is Following You: Up a Tree
events.intro:
There is somebody up a tree. They have dropped a notebook.
It lies open on the path: a drawing of your last battle, every switch marked with arrows.

success.text: When you look back, the notebook is gone, and so is the person in the tree.
A hand comes down out of the leaves, takes it, and vanishes. A very small voice says, "Thank you."

events.name: Someone Is Following You: The Stranger
events.intro:
At last they step out onto the path: a trainer about your age, notebook clutched to their chest.

Stranger: "I watched you win a battle you should have lost."
Stranger: "I want to know how."

success.text:
Stranger: "I was hoping you'd say that."
They send out three Pokémon. You know them. They are yours: the same kinds, the same moves, the same order.

They blink, as if nobody has ever said that to them.
Stranger: "...Really? Just walk? Right. Yes. I can walk."

They go red. They nod. They turn round and walk back the way they came.

You are almost sure that is the end of it.

events.name: Your Travelling Companion
events.intro:
The stranger falls in beside you at the stage gate, notebook already open.
Stranger: "I've got questions. I've numbered them. Is that all right?"

Stranger: "Why that one first? The Pokémon you lead with. Why that one?"

choices.label: "It was the first one I trusted."

success.text: They write it down, very slowly, and underline "trusted".

choices.label: "It's the one that matches up best."

success.text: They write it down, and draw a little table next to it.

events.name: Your Travelling Companion: Another Question
events.intro:
Stranger: "Do you always look at them before you pick?"
They mean your Pokémon. You had not noticed that you do.

success.text: They nod, as if that settles something important.
They write that down too. "Didn't know," underlined twice.

events.name: Your Travelling Companion: The Last Question
events.intro:
Stranger: "What do you do when you're frightened? You don't look it."
Stranger: "Is that a trick? Can I have it?"

success.text: You show them how you breathe before a battle. They copy it badly. Then less badly.

choices.label: "I just am frightened. I go anyway."

success.text: They stop walking. They write nothing at all.

events.name: The Wanderer Steps Out
events.intro:
At the end of the stage they stop and close the notebook.
Stranger: "I think I've got it now. Most of it."
Stranger: "Show me the rest."

success.text: They lead with something just like yours, and look at it before they pick.

events.name: The One Who Follows: Why

remembers.notice: You told them to stop following you. They did, for a while. They are here anyway. They look embarrassed about it.
There is a new page at the front of the notebook: your battle, every move, and at the bottom, underlined, "how?"

events.intro:
The stranger is waiting at the side of the path. The notebook is open at the last clean page.

Stranger: "One more. The only one that matters."
Stranger: "Why do you do this?"

success.text:
They write it down, underline it, and shut the notebook for good.
Stranger: "Then I'll race you. Next region. Every stage."

You look at your team. They watch you look. They write it down, underline it, and shut the notebook for good.
Stranger: "Then maybe we don't have to be enemies. Next region, I'll find out."

They stare at you. Then they laugh, properly, for the first time.
Stranger: "Me neither."
They write it down, underline it, and shut the notebook for good.

Stranger: "Then I'll keep watching. Next region. Closer, this time."

events.name: The One Who Follows: A Rival Now

remembers.intro:
The stranger is waiting at the stage gate with two cups of something hot.
Stranger: "For them, you said. I've been trying it. It's harder than winning."
Stranger: "Battle me anyway? Friendly."

The stranger is waiting at the stage gate with a brand-new notebook, still blank.
Stranger: "You didn't know yet. Do you know now?"
Stranger: "Show me. I'll take notes."

events.intro:
The stranger is waiting at the stage gate, already warmed up, already counting.
Stranger: "To win, you said. So: race. Me first."

success.text: They do not look at their Pokémon before they pick. Then, after a second, they do.

events.name: Emptied Shelves

remembers.notice: Shopkeeper: "Said they were stocking up for the League."

Shopkeeper: "They looked frightened, honestly."
She says it gently, as if it might be catching.

events.intro:
The shopkeeper is wringing her hands before you are through the door.
Shopkeeper: "Your friend. The one in all the papers. They came in this morning."

Shopkeeper: "Paid in full. Very polite. Took everything."
Every Poké Ball. Every Revive. The shelves behind her are bare to the wood.

success.text:
A detour, then. The next town's shop is a node out of your way.
Their shelves, at least, are full.

She thinks, then fetches a box from the back: a few Great Balls, honest stock, at a fair price.
Shopkeeper: "Regular's discount. You look like you'll be a regular."

Shopkeeper: "Went east. Two nodes, I'd say. They had a cart."

Their camp is on your map now, a little further along.

events.name: Emptied Shelves: The Haul

remembers.notice: {rival}: "It's the League. You stock for the League. Everybody knows that."

They do not look up.
{rival}: "I keep thinking: what if I run out. In the middle. With you watching."

events.intro:
A camp. Forty Poké Balls in rows. Revives stacked like bricks.
{rival} is counting them. They lose count. They start again.

success.text:
They push half of it across to you with their foot.
{rival}: "...I'd have sold them back to you. At a mark-up."
{rival}: "I thought about it. I'm telling you so you know I thought about it."

{rival}: "Fine. Winner takes the lot."
They stack the crates behind them like a wall.

They stare at you. Then at the haul. Then, slowly, they stop counting.
{rival}: "...Right. Thanks."
They mean it more than they would like to.

events.name: A Care Package
events.intro:
At the Center, the nurse slides a paper bag across the counter.
Poké Balls. A lot of them. Some still have the price stickers from that shop. There is no note.

success.text: You do not need a note. You know whose handwriting it would have been.

events.name: Emptied Shelves: Never Again
events.intro:
{rival} passes you outside a shop with exactly one Poké Ball in their hand.
{rival}: "One. I bought one. I'm never doing that again."
{rival}: "Don't say anything."

success.text: You say nothing. They look grateful, and a little annoyed that you managed it.

events.name: A Gift You Should Question

remembers.notice: They gave you half a shelf of Balls back, once, with their foot. This does not feel like that.

events.intro:
A box on your bed at the inn, with {rival}'s handwriting on the tag.
The wrapping is too neat.

The knot is a sailor's knot.
{rival} cannot tie a sailor's knot. You have watched them try.

success.text:
A Lucky Egg, warm in your hand. It is a good gift. It is a very good gift.
You do not notice the faint, slow blink under the lining.

Under the lining: a disc the size of a coin. It is warm. It blinks, slowly.
{lead} growls at it.

You prise it out and crush it under your heel. The Lucky Egg you keep.

You find the blinking disc, and leave it right where it is.
Tomorrow you will put the whole box somewhere useful.

You find them at the Center and hold up the box.
{rival}: "I didn't wrap it. A sponsor asked me to pass it on."
{rival}: "They've been very generous. Why?"

events.name: A Gift You Should Question: The Blink
events.intro:
Something in your bag blinks. Slowly. Then the bushes on both sides of the path stand up.
Grunt: "There you are. Right where the little light said."

On the board at the last Center, the Rival Report: {rival}, smiling, shaking hands with someone in a good coat. Accepting more help.

success.text: They come out of the bushes three at a time.

events.name: A Gift You Should Question: A Stump
events.intro:
You leave the gift on a stump and step back into the trees.

Six Grunts. A net. A great deal of shouting. A stump.
Grunt: "It's a stump."
Another Grunt: "It's THEIR stump."

Behind them, unguarded: their camp. And on a crate, a ledger.

success.text:
Payments, in neat columns. Gifts, passed through a sponsor. The sponsor's name, again and again:
{lieutenant}, of {evil}.

events.name: A Gift You Should Question: The Sponsor

success.text:
They do not argue. They take the sponsor's pin off their collar and look at it for a long time.

{rival}: "{say event||champion-chaser::I thought somebody finally thought I was worth it.||prodigy::Of course. Nobody gives anything for nothing. I should have done the sums.||underdog::They said they believed in me. Nobody's ever said that before. I wanted it to be true.||bitter-challenger::Figures. The only people who ever backed me wanted something.}"
They put the pin on the ground, carefully, like something that might go off.

Then they walk to the square, where the sponsor is waiting, and hand back every gift in front of everyone.

remembers.notice: You still have the crushed disc from the gift box in your bag. You have not told them about it yet.
"A sponsor asked me to pass it on," they said, back then. They said it so happily.

events.intro:
{rival} is in a new coat. A good coat. There is a small pin on the collar: {evil}'s mark, if you know where to look.
{rival}: "My sponsor sends their regards. Isn't it great? Somebody finally noticed."

success.text:
Their face closes like a door.
{rival}: "You're jealous."
{rival}: "Somebody finally backs me, and you can't stand it."

They walk off with the pin still on. They will find out at the climax. On the wrong side.

You say nothing. They straighten the pin and go.
You will be there when they find out. You will have to be.
